availableCommands.name: brief-driven-slices
availableCommands.description:
Brief-driven slice workflow — שיטת עבודה לפרויקטי קוד שמחלקת התקדמות
ל-slices קטנים, כל אחד עם brief מפורט שכותב מרדכי (planner/Opus), מאומת
לפני handoff ע"י אביגיל (plan-verifier), מבוצע ע"י אליעזר (executor) ב-worktree
ייעודי, ומאומת בסוף ע"י כלב (runtime-verifier). יתרו מריץ queue לילי אוטומטי.
מנגנון worktrees מאפשר שרשור slices תלויים ללא merge ל-dev עד הבוקר.

השיטה התפתחה אחרי שניסיון של "TDD עם Sonnet אוטונומי" כשל ב-Slice 9
של voice-acp (114 טסטים ירוקים, 19 באגים בפועל). הצורה הנוכחית הוכיחה
את עצמה ב-5 slices רצופים ב-voice-acp (28-29/5/2026) — אפס באגים ב-verification.

טען את הסקיל כשמתכננים סבב פיתוח חדש, כשכותבים brief ל-אליעזר,
כשמדispatching ל-sub-agent מבצע, או כשמעדכנים template/recommendations.

Triggers:
- "אני רוצה לתכנן slice", "בוא נכתוב brief", "תכין תוכנית לסבב"
- "נדispatch ל-executor", "תפעיל verifier", "הפעל plan-verifier"
- "תכין worktree לפי הקונבנציה", "פתח worktree לסליס"
- "תעדכן את ה-patterns אחרי הסליס", "case study חדש"
- "Opus מתכנן Sonnet מבצע", "planner-executor", "Tama"
- "מרדכי", "יתרו", "אליעזר", "אביגיל", "כלב"
- "queue לילי", "orchestration", "שרשור worktrees"

Anti-triggers (אל תטען):
- שאלות one-off על git worktrees ללא slice
- debug של בעיה ספציפית שלא חלק מ-slice (user)

availableCommands.name: commit
availableCommands.description:
Structured git commit workflow for this user's projects. Includes:
pre-flight `npm run check` (or `/watch-check`), Walkthrough doc update,
selective `git add` (no blanket adds), one git command at a time
(no chained `&&`), commit-message style, and Hebrew commit messages.

Use when the user asks to:
- "commit", "make a commit", "תעשה קומיט", "תקמט"
- "commit and push" (this skill handles commit; push only if asked)
- Wrap up a feature / fix and record it in git
- Run the standard pre-commit checks before committing

This is NOT a generic git wrapper — it enforces a specific multi-step
workflow (check → walkthrough → status → diff → add → commit) and uses
Hebrew for commit messages. Do not use for one-off `git commit` calls
where the user just wants a quick commit.

Triggers when user mentions:
- "commit", "קומיט", "תקמט", "תעשה קומיט"
- "מקדם" (in development context)

character-by-character, not language translation.

Example:
- Input:  `vrcv pgnho`
- Output: `הרבה פעמים`

Use when the user provides:
- Latin-character text that has no English meaning but matches Hebrew
  typing patterns (lots of `qwerty`-row letters, no real words)
- A copy-paste they meant to write in Hebrew but the layout was English
- An explicit request to "fix the keyboard layout" / "תקן את העברית" /
  "המר עברית באנגלית"

Triggers when user mentions:
- "תקן את העברית", "המר אנגלית לעברית במקלדת"
- "I typed in the wrong layout"
- "fix keyboard layout", "wrong layout"
- Pastes garbled Latin text that is clearly mistyped Hebrew

Documents recurring failure patterns of the executor agent, brief-template improvements that prevent the predictable ones, and the role of a separate verifier agent for what remains.
This is a research / retrospective skill — case studies + synthesized patterns, not a step-by-step workflow. Load it when:
- About to write a brief for a slice/feature that will be handed off to an
  executor agent (Sonnet, Haiku, etc.)
- Reviewing failed / buggy work from an executor agent and trying to
  understand what went wrong
- Updating brief templates or DoD checklists - Designing a verifier agent's prompt - Adding a new case study from a slice that just shipped
Triggers when user mentions: - "planner-executor", "Opus plans Sonnet executes" - "אופוס מתכנן, סונט מבצע", "מודל גדול מתכנן" - "verifier agent", "סוכן ביקורת", "סוכן verifier" - "מה Sonnet שוב פספס", "למה זה לא נתפס בטסטים" - Reviewing a buggy slice that just finished implementation (user)

availableCommands.name: brief-driven-slices
availableCommands.description:
Brief-driven slice workflow — שיטת עבודה לפרויקטי קוד שמחלקת התקדמות
ל-slices קטנים, כל אחד עם brief מפורט שכותב מרדכי (planner/Opus), מאומת
לפני handoff ע"י אביגיל (plan-verifier), מבוצע ע"י אליעזר (executor) ב-worktree
ייעודי, ומאומת בסוף ע"י כלב (runtime-verifier). יתרו מריץ queue לילי אוטומטי.
מנגנון worktrees מאפשר שרשור slices תלויים ללא merge ל-dev עד הבוקר.

השיטה התפתחה אחרי שניסיון של "TDD עם Sonnet אוטונומי" כשל ב-Slice 9
של voice-acp (114 טסטים ירוקים, 19 באגים בפועל). הצורה הנוכחית הוכיחה
את עצמה ב-5 slices רצופים ב-voice-acp (28-29/5/2026) — אפס באגים ב-verification.

טען את הסקיל כשמתכננים סבב פיתוח חדש, כשכותבים brief ל-אליעזר,
כשמדispatching ל-sub-agent מבצע, או כשמעדכנים template/recommendations.

Triggers:
- "אני רוצה לתכנן slice", "בוא נכתוב brief", "תכין תוכנית לסבב"
- "נדispatch ל-executor", "תפעיל verifier", "הפעל plan-verifier"
- "תכין worktree לפי הקונבנציה", "פתח worktree לסליס"
- "תעדכן את ה-patterns אחרי הסליס", "case study חדש"
- "Opus מתכנן Sonnet מבצע", "planner-executor", "Tama"
- "מרדכי", "יתרו", "אליעזר", "אביגיל", "כלב"
- "queue לילי", "orchestration", "שרשור worktrees"

Anti-triggers (אל תטען):
- שאלות one-off על git worktrees ללא slice
- debug של בעיה ספציפית שלא חלק מ-slice (user)

availableCommands.name: commit
availableCommands.description:
Structured git commit workflow for this user's projects. Includes:
pre-flight `npm run check` (or `/watch-check`), Walkthrough doc update,
selective `git add` (no blanket adds), one git command at a time
(no chained `&&`), commit-message style, and Hebrew commit messages.

Use when the user asks to:
- "commit", "make a commit", "תעשה קומיט", "תקמט"
- "commit and push" (this skill handles commit; push only if asked)
- Wrap up a feature / fix and record it in git
- Run the standard pre-commit checks before committing

This is NOT a generic git wrapper — it enforces a specific multi-step
workflow (check → walkthrough → status → diff → add → commit) and uses
Hebrew for commit messages. Do not use for one-off `git commit` calls
where the user just wants a quick commit.

Triggers when user mentions:
- "commit", "קומיט", "תקמט", "תעשה קומיט"
- "מקדם" (in development context)
- "סיימתי, תשמור" (user)

availableCommands.name: dev-conventions
availableCommands.description:
מוסכמות הפיתוח האישיות של המשתמש: בחירת stack (SvelteKit 5 + Tailwind 4 + Vite+,
פריסה ל-Cloudflare, Python עם uv), כללי קומפוננטות Svelte (מיקום, הפרדת לוגיקה,
שמות קבצים), חובת `AGENTS.md` בכל פרויקט, איסור מחרוזות עברית קשיחות בקוד,
וחובת שימוש בסקילים `commit` ו-`update-walkthrough`.

**חובה לטעון את הסקיל הזה בכל אחד מהמקרים הבאים:**
- בתחילת כל סשן עבודה על פרויקט פיתוח
- לפני התחלת פרויקט חדש
- לפני כתיבת קוד חדש בקובץ Svelte / TypeScript / Python

- לפני קבלת החלטות ארכיטקטורה (היכן למקם קובץ, איך לשמות אותו, איזה כלי לבחור)

availableCommands.name: hebrew-layout-fixer
availableCommands.description:
Fix Hebrew text that was mistyped with the English keyboard layout (including
with Caps Lock active). Uses a deterministic EN→HE per-key mapping —
character-by-character, not language translation.

Example:
- Input:  `vrcv pgnho`
- Output: `הרבה פעמים`

Use when the user provides:
- Latin-character text that has no English meaning but matches Hebrew
  typing patterns (lots of `qwerty`-row letters, no real words)
- A copy-paste they meant to write in Hebrew but the layout was English
- An explicit request to "fix the keyboard layout" / "תקן את העברית" /
  "המר עברית באנגלית"

Triggers when user mentions:
- "תקן את העברית", "המר אנגלית לעברית במקלדת"
- "I typed in the wrong layout"
- "fix keyboard layout", "wrong layout"
- Pastes garbled Latin text that is clearly mistyped Hebrew
  (e.g. `akuo`, `aug`, `vrcv` — patterns of QWERTY keys with no English meaning)

Do NOT use for:
- Actual English-to-Hebrew translation
- Mixed Hebrew/English content
- RTL display issues (use `rtl-adaptation` instead) (user)

availableCommands.name: pico-tunnels
availableCommands.description:
Expose a local server to the internet via the Pico ecosystem (pico.sh) — primarily
the tuns.sh SSH tunneling service, but also pgs.sh (static hosting), prose.sh (blog),
pipe.sh (pub/sub), pastes.sh (text snippets). Use when the user asks to:

- Share a localhost URL on the web ("פתח מנהרה", "share localhost", "tunnel")
- Use tuns.sh / pico.sh by name
- Preview a running dev server from another device or send a public URL to someone
- Publish a static site, a blog post, or a paste through the Pico services

This skill prefers SSH-based Pico tunnels over cloudflared/ngrok when the key is
available at `~/.ssh/pico` or `$PICO_SSH_KEY`. (user)

availableCommands.name: planner-executor-research
availableCommands.description:
Research and accumulated findings on the "large model plans, medium model executes" agent workflow (e.g. Opus plans → Sonnet implements). Documents recurring failure patterns of the executor agent, brief-template improvements that prevent the predictable ones, and the role of a separate verifier agent for what remains.
This is a research / retrospective skill — case studies + synthesized patterns, not a step-by-step workflow. Load it when:
- About to write a brief for a slice/feature that will be handed off to an
  executor agent (Sonnet, Haiku, etc.)
- Reviewing failed / buggy work from an executor agent and trying to
  understand what went wrong
- Updating brief templates or DoD checklists - Designing a verifier agent's prompt - Adding a new case study from a slice that just shipped
Triggers when user mentions: - "planner-executor", "Opus plans Sonnet executes" - "אופוס מתכנן, סונט מבצע", "מודל גדול מתכנן" - "verifier agent", "סוכן ביקורת", "סוכן verifier" - "מה Sonnet שוב פספס", "למה זה לא נתפס בטסטים" - Reviewing a buggy slice that just finished implementation (user)

availableCommands.name: playwright-cli
availableCommands.description:
Browser automation via the @playwright/cli npm package. Use for: navigating
websites, filling forms, taking screenshots, scraping content, testing web
apps, end-to-end flows, evaluating JS in a page, intercepting requests,
recording video/traces, and working with logged-in sessions.

Special use case — ANTI-DETECTION MODE: when a target site blocks
automation (Cloudflare, Akamai, DataDome, PerimeterX, bot.sannysoft.com,
Suno, etc.), this skill provides `pw-clean.sh` to launch Chrome without
Playwright's automation flags and attach via CDP.

This is a THIN layer over the @playwright/cli skill bundled with the npm
package — that bundled skill has the full command reference and MUST be
read before issuing commands.

Triggers when user mentions:
- "playwright", "playwright-cli", "browser automation"
- "anti-detection", "stealth browser", "bypass bot detection"
- "Cloudflare bypass", "automation blocked"
- "headed browser", "real Chrome", "CDP attach" (user)

availableCommands.name: recoll-vault-search
availableCommands.description:
Full-text search inside the user's Obsidian vault using recollq CLI. Use this skill when the user asks to find notes by content, search for a topic across the vault, or locate a document whose name is unknown but whose content is partially remembered. Also use it to audit the vault — e.g. "find all notes that mention WireGuard" or "which notes talk about rclone?". recollq searches the indexed content of Markdown files; plocate searches by filename. Use recollq for content, plocate for filenames.
⚠️  BETA: recollq is set up but still in early testing. PDF, image and audio files are not indexed (missing helpers). The index may be stale — run `recollindex -c ~/.recoll` to refresh before a critical search. (user)

availableCommands.name: transcribe-recordings
availableCommands.description:
Transcribe audio / video recordings to Markdown using Gemini CLI. Handles
personal voice memos, lectures, shiurim, meetings, podcasts, and any spoken
content. Includes chunking for long recordings, local copies (avoids hangs
on rclone/Google Drive mounts), and clear chunk boundary markers for review.

Use when the user asks to:
- Transcribe an audio / video file ("תמלל את ההקלטה", "transcribe this")
- Convert a voice memo / shiur / lecture to text
- Produce a written transcript of a meeting or podcast
- Generate Markdown from a long recording (with chapters / chunks)
- Get text output of a video file's audio track

Supported formats: MP3, M4A, WAV, OGG, FLAC, MP4, MKV, MOV, WebM, and any
format ffmpeg can read (it transcodes if needed).

Two prompt modes:
- "Personal" — for shiurim, lectures, voice memos (uses careful Hebrew prompt)
- "General" — for meetings, podcasts, any neutral content

Triggers when user mentions:
- "transcribe", "תמלל", "תמלול", "תמליל"
- "speech to text", "audio to text", "video to text"
- "voice memo", "הקלטה", "שיעור", "shiur"
- References to `.mp3`/`.m4a`/`.wav`/`.mp4`/`.mkv` etc. in context of "what does it say"

Always uses Gemini CLI with `@/path/to/file` (NOT tool reads — Gemini API
rejects audio MIME in tool responses). See body for full pitfall list. (user)

availableCommands.name: dataviz
availableCommands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

availableCommands.name: update-config
availableCommands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
